The '''2022 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final''' was a [[hurling]] match that was played on 5 June at [[Semple Stadium]] in [[Thurles]]. It was contested by [[2021 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final|defending]] champions [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] and [[Clare county hurling team|Clare]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/munster-gaa-hurling-senior-championship/fixtures|title=2022 Munster Hurling Final|date=22 May 2022|work=GAA.ie|accessdate=23 May 2022}}</ref>

The game was televised live on [[RTÉ 2]] as part of ''[[The Sunday Game]]'', presented by [[Joanne Cantwell]]. Commentary on the game was provided by [[Marty Morrissey]] alongside [[Michael Duignan (hurler)|Michael Duignan]].

Limerick, captained by [[Declan Hannon]], retained the title for the fourth year in a row after a 1-19 to 0-29 win after extra-time. The teams had been level on 14 occasions during the ninety minutes.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.skysports.com/gaa/hurling/news/30554/12628219/limerick-1-29-clare-0-29-treaty-win-fourth-munster-title-in-a-row-after-epic-extra-time-victory|title= Limerick 1-29 Clare 0-29: Treaty win fourth Munster title in a row after epic extra-time victory|date=5 June 2022|work=Sky Sports|accessdate=7 June 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2022/0605/1303148-munster-shc-final-clare-v-limerick-updates/|title= Munster SHC recap: Clare 0-29 Limerick 1-29 (aet)|date=5 June 2022|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=7 June 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://munster.gaa.ie/event/munster-senior-hurling-championship-final/|title= 2022 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final – Limerick 1-29 Clare 0-29|date=5 June 2022|work=Munster GAA|accessdate=7 June 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2022/0605/1303110-limerick-edge-past-clare-in-munster-final-classic/|title=Limerick edge Clare in extra-time epic to win fourth Munster Championship in a row|date=7 June 2022|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=7 April 2023}}</ref>

==Build-up==
The winning team were the first winners of the new [[Mick Mackey]] Cup. The two teams were meeting in the Munster final for the first time since [[1995 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|1995]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2022/0526/1301293-munster-final-terrace-tickets-sell-out-in-11-minutes/|title=Munster hurling final tickets sell out in 11 minutes|date=26 May 2022|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=26 May 2022}}</ref>

Limerick were bidding to win the Munster title for a fourth successive year with Clare looking for a first Munster title since [[1998 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final|1998]].
This was the 60th championship game between the two counties, Limerick had 37 wins to Clare’s 20 with two draws, from the previous 59.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://munster.gaa.ie/event/munster-senior-hurling-championship-final/|title=2022 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|date=5 June 2022|work=Munster GAA|accessdate=5 April 2023}}</ref>

On 26 May, the Munster Council confirmed that the final was a sell-out after 11,000 Terrace Tickets sold out in 11 minutes.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/munster-hurling-final-tickets-5774595-May2022/|title=Munster hurling final terrace tickets sell out in 11 minutes|date=26 May 2022|work=The 42|accessdate=26 May 2022}}</ref>
